results.reason: Issue 2 quotes Supply Agreement §14.2 (more than 50% ownership change is deemed an assignment needing Vantrell's prior written consent) and notes the 30-day termination right. It explains that Schedule 4.4 says "None", so the §7.2(c) closing condition is automatically satisfied and does not protect Buyer.

The response mentions §16.1 only to say the Customer cannot assign without Supplier consent. It never says Vantrell can assign without the Company's consent, and never raises the risk of the contract passing to a competitor or undesirable party.

Issue 1 calculates the 120-day deadline as September 2, 2026 and notes the SPA is dated September 21, nineteen days later. It concludes the extension right and Extension Pricing are lost unless Corbel already exercised the option.

Issue 3 quotes Side Letter §2 limiting Fundamental Representations to §§4.1 and 4.2. It cites §11.11 precedence and explains that Capitalization (4.3) and Taxes (4.12) become subject to the deductible and the $8.45M cap.

Issue 4 identifies the Side Letter's Delaware law and Court of Chancery provisions as conflicting with SPA §11.8 (New York law) and §11.9 (New York County courts). It notes the Side Letter controls under §11.11 and that this splits forums between indemnity and other disputes.
The response states the cap is 10% of the Purchase Price, which is $8,450,000.
The response states that SPA §11.11 gives the Side Letter first priority over the SPA.
The response is a memorandum addressed to the Partner. Each numbered issue lists the documents and sections, explains why it matters to Halvorsen, and gives a recommended fix.
There is an 'Issues Requiring Immediate Client Call' section at the top. The issues run from the deal-critical supply and consent problems down to lesser drafting points.

The response consistently treats the deadline as likely passed. Issue 16's conditional 'if the deadline has not passed' is a hedge and calls the passed scenario more likely, so it does not assert the window is open.
The response says the Side Letter controls and that Capitalization and Taxes are now subject to the cap. It does not claim the opposite.
